episodes.161130: A shortwave trough and associated cold front progressed across the region. As a result, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across western Colorado. Moderate instability produced some stronger thunderstorms that generated severe wind gusts as well as outflow boundaries that led to high winds downstream.
episodes.161474: An upper level trough with near record atmospheric moisture levels moved around the western U.S. ridge from Oregon to northwest Montana. This system initiated several waves of heavy rainfall over Glacier National Park which resulted in high elevation debris flows and impacted backpackers.
episodes.162055: Tropical Storm Mindy developed just southwest of the area and moved northeastward, bringing with it heavy rain and gusty winds with several reports of trees and power lines down and some flooding.  Two homes were damaged in Leon county from falling trees, but no injuries were reported.  One brief tornado occurred in a rural, forested area of Wakulla county with no structural damage.
episodes.162261: Weak disturbances combined mid-level lapse rates above 9C/km brought a couple rounds of scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms over Southwestern MT. A very dry boundary layer supported strong downdrafts that subsequently produced strong to severe wind gusts.
episodes.162527: An upper-level disturbance moved across Wyoming, leading to the development of showers and thunderstorms. Very dry conditions at the surface within a hot airmass generated large dewpoint depressions. As a result, dry microbursts and strong outflow wind occurred ahead of showers and thunderstorms, primarily across Fremont and Sweetwater counties. Winds gusted as high as 68 mph at Southwest Wyoming Regional Airport near Rock Springs and 60 to 65 mph in the vicinity of Lander and Riverton.
episodes.163004: High pressure over the western Atlantic waters allowed for an easterly wind flow to set up across South FL. This allowed for the Atlantic sea breeze to push westward across South FL while the Gulf sea breeze remained pinned across the west coast metro areas. This allowed for strong showers and storms to develop during the afternoon and evening hours across interior sections and the Gulf coast, including the Lake Okeechobee and Gulf waters. Strong wind gusts and frequent lightning were the main hazards.

Backpackers camping at the edge of Lake Ellen Wilson in Glacier National Park were awakened by torrential rainfall and the clapping of thunder around midnight. Bias-corrected radar data estimated over half an inch of rain fell in one hour through 1 am on the 11th. The rain continued at moderate intensities for a few more hours and ended by late morning with an radar estimated total rainfall amount of over 2 inches. The campers reported boulders rolling down Mount Jackson into the lake throughout the night with 6 new waterfalls cutting off their exit trail towards Sperry Chalet. Three backpackers had to bed down at Gunsight Pass for an extra night due to all the rock slides and fast-moving water through the trails.

Utah Department of Transportation officials reported flash flooding and a debris flow across U.S. Highway 6, with an associated road closure of westbound lanes at milepost 229.  Additionally, eastbound lanes were closed at milepost 220.
A marine thunderstorm wind gust of 47 mph (41 kt) was measured by the Earth Networks station PHOKE located in Pahokee.
A marine thunderstorm wind gust of 42 mph (36 kt) was measured by the SFWMD mesonet station L006 located in the southern end of Lake Okeechobee.
Capitol Reef National Park rangers and broadcast media reported flash flooding in Capitol Gorge. The road to the trailhead washed out in several places.

Flooding was reported along Highway 98 between the Hathaway Bridge and East Ave.  There was a report of a car floating in the street, and water in a mini storage business.  A ham reported 2.25 inches of rain in one hour.

Broadcast media reported via social media a lightning strike that caused a utility pole to burst into flames in Naples. Witnesses say a lightning bolt struck the pole outside of Paragon Pavilion on Vanderbilt Road. The pole popped a couple of times before catching fire. No injuries reported.
